subject: MSA / Order Form — IP, training & feedback license clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@neptune-analytics.com>
To: tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com
Cc: procurement@neptune-analytics.com, legal@neptune-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MSA & Order Form — IP / Training clarifications

Hi Tessa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we had a productive internal sync. Attached are our annotated redlines to the MSA and the order form focused on two areas we need clarified: (1) customer output ownership and any assignment/attribution requirements; and (2) explicit language around training the model on our data / feedback (we prefer an opt-in model for training and a limited feedback license).

Key asks:
- Confirm whether Redwood will claim any ownership rights over output generated by Neptune users or require assignment.
- If training is allowed, we need: opt-in checkbox/process, data deletion/retention windows, and a prohibition on using outputs for model improvement without express consent.

I attached a short redline with inline comments and a summary PDF. Can you route to legal and procurement and tell us what level of compromise Redwood typically accepts for enterprise deals? We are on a tight timeline for Q3 procurement signoff.

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Sr. Product Counsel, Neptune Analytics
Attachments: Neptune_MSA_redlines_20270822.docx (docx), Neptune_OrderForm_diff_notes.pdf (pdf)
From: tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com, laura.bennett@redwood-inference.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Training clarifications

Alice — really appreciate the clear redlines and the summary. Looping in Rishi and Laura from legal to give proposed language and options.

Quick logistics:
- We can provide a narrow "outputs are owned by the customer" clause. Need to confirm how you want attribution/attribution notice handled (we typically include a non-assertion of ownership by Redwood but request a limited license for telemetry).
- Training: our standard approach is opt-out by default for hosted, but for enterprise we support explicit opt-in with controls. We will propose retention windows and an explicit feedback license carveout for Neptune.

I will consolidate candidate language and send back by EOD tomorrow. If procurement needs a DocuSign path, let me know and I can surface it.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood-inference.com

Cc: markus.klein@redwood-inference.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: MSA & Order Form — IP / Training clarifications

Tessa / Laura — forwarding Neptune's redlines. Below are two proposed options that keep us protected while being acceptable commercially: 

Option A (preferred, low-risk):
- Output ownership: Add clause: "Customer retains ownership of Outputs they provide or receive; Redwood makes no ownership claim over Customer Outputs. Customer grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, revocable license to use telemetry and aggregated system metrics for product operation, debugging, and service improvement. Such telemetry shall be de-identified and not used to train models for commercial redistribution without explicit written consent."

- Training / Feedback license: Add an opt-in toggle in the order form and a defined retention window (60 days) after which Neptune data is purged from any model-improvement pipelines. Include requirement that any training on Neptune data will require a separate SOW or written consent.

Option B (concession path):
- Allow a slightly broader telemetry license (includes narrowly-scoped feature-flagged experiments) and extend retention to 90 days. Require Neptune to sign an addendum for any production model retraining.

Attachments: draft para text (RI-proposed-language-para.txt) — please review and advise if Option A would be acceptable commercially. If Neptune pushes back on retention, we can move to Option B.

Rgds,
Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: tessa.morgan@redwood-inference.com
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@neptune-analytics.com>, procurement@neptune-analytics.com

Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — IP / Training clarifications

Alice — thanks, and appreciate the fast turn. Per internal legal we've prepared a short suggested paragraph and two pickup options (A/B) — attached. High level summary:

- We will add explicit language confirming Customer ownership of Outputs and a non-assertion by Redwood.
- For telemetry/feedback we propose a narrow operational telemetry license (de-identified) and an opt-in path for any training or model improvements using Neptune data.
- Retention: Option A = 60 days; Option B = 90 days + addendum for retraining.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached proposed paragraph (RI-proposed-language-para.txt) and tell us which option you prefer.
2) If Option A is acceptable, we can integrate it into the order form and send a DocuSign for signature this week (DocuSign link included).

Attachments: RI-proposed-language-para.txt (text)
DocuSign: https://app.docusign.com/Neptune-DEAL-4591

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20 min call if you want to walk through tradeoffs (Rishi can join).

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales Lead | Redwood Inference

Tessa / Rishi / Laura — we reviewed Option A overnight and it aligns with Neptune's legal requirements. Two quick clarifications before we sign:
1) Can you add a single sentence explicitly stating "Redwood will not use Customer Outputs for model training or improvement unless Neptune provides prior written consent" (we want that sentence in the MSA body, not buried in an appendix).
2) For the 60 day retention window, can you confirm the mechanism for purging (we prefer a contractual commitment plus a short audit log sample).

If you can add that sentence and share a sample purge/audit clause, procurement is ready to accept and DocuSign this week. Thanks for working quickly — appreciate the collaborative approach.

--
Alice Chen
